concept.name: Option
concept.definition: A contract giving its holder the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an underlying interest at a strike price by or at expiration, while the writer bears the corresponding obligation if exercised.
concept.intuition: It defines the legal and economic claim being traded, including who must perform and when.
concept.mechanics: The buyer pays premium; value depends on underlying price, strike, time, volatility, rates, and contract style; exercise or settlement follows the contract rules.
concept.formula: Call payoff at expiry = max(underlying price - strike, 0); put payoff = max(strike - underlying price, 0)
concept.failure_modes: Counterparty, settlement, liquidity, exercise, basis, and leverage terms differ by venue and contract and can dominate the apparent payoff.
concept.misconceptions: Similar price exposure does not make spot, forwards, futures, and options operationally or legally interchangeable.
concept.example: A 100-strike call expires with $8 intrinsic value when the underlying settles at $108, before subtracting premium.
